# Constant profiles disprove universal three-Grunbaum credit

The all-tent theorem does not extend to all concave planar profiles.
The obstruction already uses one affine piece per profile, so the
six-piece reduction remains valid but cannot prove the false target.
This is not a counterexample to (OC), nor to the weaker hollow-edge
credit involving the actual middle-fiber mass.

## 1. An exact rational body and an actual oblique halfspace

Let

    A=[-1/2,1/2] times[-1/2,1/2],
    B=[-1,1] times[-1/4,1/4],
    K=M=(A+B)/2=[-3/4,3/4] times[-3/8,3/8].

Both endpoint areas are1; the middle area is9/8. All three ordinary
centroids are zero. The full-dimensional convex body

    C=conv(({-1} times A) union({1} times B))

has exactly these three integer fibers, because its middle slice is
their Minkowski average. Its induced mixed area is25/8. The averaged
endpoint-centroid candidate is the actual point y=(0,0,0).

Take the closed ambient halfspace

    H={(z,s,t):s+z/2>=0}.

At z=-1 it meets A in the supporting edge s=1/2, of area0; this
boundary trace is nonempty and has not been replaced by an empty set.
At z=1 it cuts B at s=-1/2 and has area3/4. At z=0 it takes half
of M, of area9/16. Therefore

    |S intersect H|_MI=21/16=4/3-1/48.                (1)

The directional profiles are simply f=1 on[-1/2,1/2] and
g=1/2 on[-1,1]. Their integral and mean constraints are exact.
Their supremal convolution realizes M exactly, so(1) also disproves
the unrestricted functional assertion J_alpha>=4/3 at alpha=1/2.
There is no centroid mismatch in this example.

## 2. The complete width family and its exact directional minimum

For R>=1 keep A as above and put

    B_R=[-R/2,R/2] times[-1/(2R),1/(2R)].

The midpoint area and its positive axial cap are

    m_R=(R+2+1/R)/4,   Q_R=m_R/2.

In the common proper range -1/2<=alpha<=1/2 the endpoint cap sum is

    P_R(alpha)=1-alpha(1-1/R).

For alpha>=1/2 the A cap is empty in area and the B cap increases
until it is full. For alpha<=-1/2 the A cap is full and the combined
area is at least1. Thus the exact all-tilt minimum is

    min_alpha P_R(alpha)=1/2+1/(2R),
    min_alpha J_R(alpha)=R/8+3/4+5/(8R).                (2)

The second expression has minimum(3+sqrt5)/4 at R=sqrt5. Its
difference from4/3 is

    [(3R-5)(R-3)]/(24R).

Hence every R in(5/3,3) gives an actual counterexample to the
universal4/3 whole-cap claim; R=2 is the rational certificate above.
No numerical optimization is used in these conclusions.

## 3. Even selecting another center does not rescue that absolute target

The example also rules out a universal ANY-center raw-depth bound4/3
for equal-area arbitrary planar endpoints. It is invariant under the
continuous reflection (z,s,t)->(z,-s,-t). On the middle fiber its
raw halfspace depth is therefore even. It is also quasiconcave:
if y lies on the segment joining y_1,y_2, every containing halfspace
contains at least one of y_1,y_2, and its mass is at least the minimum
of their two depths. Thus D(y)>=min(D(y_1),D(y_2)). Taking the midpoint
of x and-x shows that the middle-fiber maximum is attained at0.
Equation(1) bounds that maximum above by21/16.

On an extreme fiber, any ordinary cap through a candidate can be
isolated from the two other compact fibers by adding a sufficiently
large integer-normal component. An ordinary halfplane through that
candidate has area at most1/2 in its rectangular fiber (choose one
of two complementary through-point halfplanes). Consequently the raw
depth of every extreme-fiber point is at most1/2. Therefore

    max_(y in S) D_S(y)<=21/16<4/3.                    (3)

No all-direction lower bound or exact global depth is claimed. The
explicit cap and the quasiconcavity argument suffice for the strict
upper bound in(3). The OC target here is only(2/9)(25/8)=25/36,
and is not contradicted.

## 4. What remains of the motivating edge problem

In the hollow base 2 Delta_2 with vertex-fiber areas v and midpoint-
fiber areas k, the total mass is3(v+k) and the occupied-parity target
is(3/4)Gamma_d(v+k). An actual anchored edge has endpoint areas v,v
and middle area k. Thus its needed credit is

    D_edge >=(3/4)Gamma_d(v+k),                         (4)

not the stronger mass-independent3Gamma_d v. For1<=k/v<=5/3,
the standard averaged-endpoint-centroid credit2Gamma_d v already
pays(4); for k/v>=3 an ordinary centroid of the middle fiber does.
Those two lower bounds alone leave the scalar interval5/3<k/v<3.
The rectangle example has k/v=9/8 and does not obstruct(4).

The proved triangle-endpoint theorem pays(4) throughout that interval,
but the constant-profile obstruction forbids extending its absolute
raw4v/3 conclusion to arbitrary convex endpoint bodies. Any new
extension must retain the actual middle body/mass or select another
valid center with a separately proved budget. Such a budget is now
proved at the TRUE mixed centroid, for arbitrary equal-volume endpoint
bodies in every continuous dimension, in
`candidate 660db01ed45063dd`.
It uses the actual dominated midpoint coupling and the mass-dependent
centroid inequality. Thus the weaker edge target is no longer an open
claim in this collection; the fixed-center and absolute-constant
obstructions proved here retain their stated scope.


## 5. The actual midpoint-volume calibration

Eliminating R from(2), with m=m_R>=1, gives

    R=2m-1+2sqrt(m(m-1)),
    J_rect(m)=3m/2-sqrt(m(m-1)).                        (5)

Thus any universal lower bound for the averaged-centroid whole-cap
functional based only on the actual midpoint area m must lie at most
at this curve on the rectangle family. By Section3 the same curve is
an upper bound for the globally best raw depth in that family; equality
in all directions is not needed and is not asserted. The family does
not obstruct the desired edge curve(m+1)/3, since

    (7m-2)^2-36m(m-1)=13m^2+8m+4>0,

so J_rect(m)>(m+1)/3 for every m>=1. No reduction from arbitrary
middle K to its exact midpoint M follows from this calculation.

## 6. The weaker edge target also needs more than the fixed averaged center

Keep the rational rectangles A,B,M from Section1, but replace the middle
fiber by the actual convex pentagon

    K=conv(M,(-17/3,0)).

The added region is precisely a triangle attached to the left vertical
side of M. Its area is

    (1/2)(3/4)(17/3-3/4)=59/32,

so k=|K|=9/8+59/32=95/32. All of K at s>=-3/4 coincides with M;
in particular its positive-s cap still has area9/16. The same closed
ambient cap H={s+z/2>=0} through the actual averaged endpoint centroid
therefore still has mass21/16=126/96. The desired edge credit is now

    (3/4)Gamma_2(k+1)=(k+1)/3=127/96.                 (6)

Thus that SPECIFIED center fails the weaker target by1/96, within the
previously unresolved interval5/3<k<3. The bare ordinary-centroid
estimate Gamma_2 k=95/72 is also short of(6), by1/288. This comparison
is only a limitation of those two explicit lower estimates: it is not
an upper bound on the depth at g_K, and it is not a counterexample to
the existence of another center satisfying(6).

The convex body conv(({-1}times A) union({0}times K) union({1}times B))
has exactly the stated integer fibers, since K contains M. Its ambient
interior is nonempty. All statements above therefore concern an actual
mixed-integer set, not independent scalar slice data. The OC target for
this three-fiber body is53/48 and is not contradicted.

## 7. Exact ordinary centroid depth pays the lost credit in this pentagon

The preceding example distinguishes a bare Grunbaum estimate from the
actual ordinary depth of the middle centroid. Here that distinction is
quantitatively sufficient. We prove the required all-normal calculation,
rather than checking only the horizontal cap used in Section6.

For

    1<=w<=1+1/sqrt(6),
    P_w={(X,Y):0<=X<=w, |Y|<=min(X,1)},

write T=|P_w|=2w-1. Its centroid is(g,0), where integration of its
vertical sections gives

    g=(w^2-1/3)/(2w-1).                                  (7)

In this range w/2<g<1.
The exact ordinary raw halfspace depth of this centroid is

    D_(P_w)(g,0)=g^2
       =(4/9)T+(w-1)^3(9w-5)/[9(2w-1)^2].                (8)

To prove(8), translate any containing line inward until it passes through
the centroid; this can only decrease the cap area. Reflection in Y=0
and reversing the unoriented line reduce every nonhorizontal through-
centroid line to X+tY=g with t>=0. The horizontal line gives T/2 on
each side. Let E(t)=|P_w intersect{X+tY<=g}|. Direct integration, or
the shoelace formula for the cut polygon, gives all three possible
vertex statuses:

    E(t)=g^2/(1-t^2),
        0<=t<=1-g;

    E(t)=g+(t-1)/2+g^2/[2(1+t)],
        1-g<=t<=w-g;

    E(t)=T/2+[A t-B]/[2t(1+t)],
        t>=w-g,
    A=w(2g-w)>0, B=(w-g)^2.                              (9)

For clarity, the polygon defining E(t) in the middle status has vertices
(0,0),(1,-1),(g+t,-1),(g/(1+t),g/(1+t)). In the last status
the cut meets the right edge at(w,(g-w)/t) and the upper sloping edge
at(g/(1+t),g/(1+t)); both lower vertices belong to E(t). Thus(9)
includes every support transition, not only proper cuts within a
chosen status. At w=1 the middle interval can have zero length.

The first expression increases with t. The middle derivative is
1/2-g^2/[2(1+t)^2]>0. In the last expression the derivative has the
sign of -A t^2+2Bt+B. Since A+B=g^2, its unique positive zero is

    t_*=(w-g)/(2g-w)>=w-g,

where the last inequality follows from 0<2g-w<1. It gives

    max_(t>=0) E(t)=T/2+(2g-w)^2/2.                      (10)

After this maximum E(t) decreases to T/2. Consequently
min E(t)=min(g^2,T/2), while min(T-E(t)) equals
P_*=T/2-(2g-w)^2/2. The exact identity

    P_*-g^2
      =(w-1)^2[1-6(w-1)^2]/[6(2w-1)^2]>=0              (11)

also shows g^2<=T/2. Thus every cap through the centroid has area
at least g^2, and the apex-side vertical cap attains it. Expanding
g^2-(4/9)T gives the second identity in(8). Lines have area zero,
so these calculations apply to closed halfspaces without a boundary
mass qualification.

For the actual K of Section6, the affine map

    X=(s+17/3)/(59/12),  Y=t/(3/8)

takes K to P_(77/59) and has inverse area factor59/32. The centroid
is g_K=(-2537/1710,0); in normalized coordinates it is
(14306/16815,0). The range in the theorem holds because
6(18/59)^2<1. Hence its ACTUAL ordinary raw depth is

    D_K(g_K)=51165409/38338200,
    D_K(g_K)-(4/9)|K|=16119/1064950,
    D_K(g_K)-(k+1)/3=1788661/153352800>0.                (12)

Every ambient halfspace through(0,g_K) restricts to a containing
halfplane in K if its continuous normal is nonzero; with continuous
normal zero it contains the whole middle fiber. Thus the actual mixed
depth at(0,g_K) is at least D_K(g_K), and(12) pays the desired edge
credit for this specific compatible pentagon family. This is a proved
shape-dependent ordinary-centroid surplus, not a universal tradeoff
between endpoint-profile loss and middle-centroid surplus.

## 8. A mass-dependent surplus throughout a cone-plus-rectangle range

The line-status proof in Section7 works without (11) throughout the
larger range 1<=w<1+1/sqrt(3), where g<1. In that range it gives the
exact formula

    D_(P_w)(g,0)=min{g^2,T/2-(2g-w)^2/2}.                (13)

Indeed the minimum of E(t) is min(g^2,T/2), and the second entry in
(13) is at most T/2. No comparison between the two entries is needed.

Let M be any rectangle of area m, and let K be its convex hull with
one point on the perpendicular bisector beyond one of its sides.
Write k=|K|. Suppose

    1<=m<=4/3,             35/12<=k<=3.                 (14)

Then the actual ordinary centroid of K satisfies

    D_K(g_K)>(k+1)/3.                                  (15)

This normalization uses the same area unit as the two unit-area
endpoints; it is an ordinary statement about the indicated family.
Affine normalization of the rectangle and apex gives P_w with

    w=1+m/[2(k-m)]<=27/19<1+1/sqrt(3),
    inverse area factor=k-m.

Substitution into (13) gives exactly

    D_K(g_K)=min{D_1,D_2},
    D_1=(8k^2-4km-m^2)^2/[144k^2(k-m)],
    D_2=(32k^3+3km^2+m^3)/(72k^2).                     (16)

Both denominators are positive. The numerators after subtracting
(k+1)/3 are respectively

    N_1=16k^4-16k^3m-48k^3+48k^2m+8km^3+m^4,
    N_2=8k^3-24k^2+3km^2+m^3.                         (17)

Both are strictly positive throughout (14). For N_2 the partial
derivatives in m and k are positive because k>2. For N_1,

    partial_m N_1=16k^2(3-k)+24km^2+4m^3>0,
    (partial_k N_1)/8
      =k^2(8k-18-6m)+12km+m^3>=-24+35+m^3>0.

The last estimate uses k<=3, 8k-18-6m>=-8/3 and 12km>=35.
Thus both minima occur at(m,k)=(1,35/12), where

    N_1=3361/1296>0,       N_2=881/216>0.

This proves(15) for every continuous normal via(13), not just for
the axis of the appendage. It also supplies a mixed depth lower bound
at(0,g_K) whenever this K is an actual middle fiber.

In the reciprocal-rectangle endpoint family of Section2, the displayed
axial cap can fall below the target(k+1)/3 with k<=3 only when
5/3<R<3 and k>3J_R-1. These conditions give m_R<=4/3 and

    k>(5+3sqrt(5))/4>35/12.

Therefore every such particular axial-credit obstruction is paid by
the exact ordinary-centroid surplus (15), if K is formed by the
specified one-apex enlargement. This conclusion does not allow an
arbitrary compatible superbody K to be replaced by that enlargement.
